T: Lent is over. The chocolate shop is open.
D: A woman opens a chocolate shop in a strict French village during Lent and shakes everyone up.
P: Serve the hot chocolate when Vianne pours one for Armande.
S: Vianne's spiced hot chocolate, the old South American way
Dark chocolate melted into hot milk with a split chilli, cinnamon stick and a pinch of salt, steeped 5 minutes, strained, served in tiny cups.
the window of the chocolate shop
Dark chocolate ganache with cream and a little butter, chilled, scooped and rolled, coated in cocoa, chopped hazelnuts or chilli sugar.
the French village square on market day

Sliced saucisson, a wedge of comté, soft goat's cheese, cornichons, fig jam and walnuts on a wooden board with warm crusty baguette. Take 200g comté and 150g soft goat's cheese out of the fridge an hour ahead. Slice a 200g saucisson thinly on an angle. Warm a baguette at 180C for 5 minutes and slice. Arrange the cheeses, saucisson, a small bowl of cornichons, 3 tbsp fig jam and a handful of walnuts on a wooden board with the bread.
M: the birthday party Vianne cooks for Armande
Duck legs salted overnight, cooked slowly in their fat at 140C for 2.5 hours, crisped skin side down, with potatoes roasted in duck fat and a green salad.
River party trout with almond brown butter
the river people's party on the boats

Whole trout grilled with lemon, thyme and garlic, finished with nutty brown butter and toasted flaked almonds, with buttery new potatoes. Boil 800g new potatoes for 15 minutes and toss with butter and parsley. Stuff 4 cleaned whole trout with lemon slices, thyme and sliced garlic, brush with oil and season. Grill or barbecue for 5 to 6 minutes a side until the flesh flakes. Melt 80g butter until foaming and nut brown, add 50g flaked almonds and toast 1 minute, then add lemon juice. Spoon over the fish.
W: the shop's chocolate, all of it
Dark chocolate melted with butter, yolks whisked in, whites whipped with sugar folded through, chilled 4 hours in small cups, a little chilli salt on top.
K: a French village after Lent ends

Southern French red warmed gently with orange, cinnamon, star anise, cloves and honey, served steaming in small glasses with an orange slice. Pour a 750ml bottle of light southern French red into a saucepan with an orange cut into slices, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise, 4 cloves and 3 tbsp honey. Warm over low heat for 15 minutes without letting it boil. Strain into small heatproof glasses and add a fresh orange slice to each.

dishes.make_ahead: Infused milk up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Heat the milk with the chilli and cinnamon until steaming.
Steep off the heat for 5 minutes, then strain.
Reheat and whisk in the chocolate and salt until smooth.
Pour into tiny cups.
Heat the cream until steaming and pour over the chocolate and butter.
Stir smooth.
Chill for 3 hours until firm (included in cook time).
Scoop and roll into balls, then coat in cocoa, in chopped hazelnuts, or in sugar mixed with chilli flakes.

dishes.make_ahead: Salt the duck the day before, confit up to 2 days ahead

steps.text: Rub the duck legs with salt, thyme and garlic.
Cure in the fridge overnight (included in cook time).
Rinse and dry the legs and arrange in a snug dish.
Cook slowly in their own fat at 140C for 2.5 hours until very tender.
Cut the potatoes, toss in some of the fat and roast at 200C until golden.
Crisp the legs skin side down in a hot pan and serve with potatoes and a green salad.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Melt the chocolate with the butter and cool slightly.
Whisk in the yolks.
Whip the whites with the sugar to soft peaks and fold in.
Spoon into small cups.
Chill for 4 hours (included in cook time), then finish with flaky salt mixed with chilli flakes.
Slice one orange and cut the other into four slices for serving.
Warm the wine with the sliced orange, spices and honey over low heat without letting it boil.
Strain into small heatproof glasses and add a fresh orange slice to each.
Slice one orange and cut the other into four slices for serving.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 5 days, cool dry place

steps.text: Melt the chocolate gently over a bowl of hot water and let it cool a little.
Spoon small discs onto lined trays.
Press an almond, hazelnut, raisin and fig piece onto each disc.
Set in a cool place or the fridge (included in cook time).
Cut the peel into strips and blanch twice in boiling water, discarding the water each time.
Simmer the peel in the sugar and water until translucent and syrupy.
Drain and dry on a rack for 40 minutes.
Melt the chocolate, dip half of each strip, and set.
Whisk the cocoa and sugar into the milk in a pan and heat gently until warm and smooth, mild and sweet for small ones.
Heat the cream and pour over half the chocolate, stir smooth and chill 90 minutes for ganache.
Chill until firm (included in cook time).
Roll 12 truffles and coat in cocoa or hazelnuts.
Melt the remaining chocolate and make 12 mendiant discs topped with almonds and raisins.
Set, then pack the two dozen assorted pieces in a box tied with red ribbon.

s.note: Vianne's spiced hot chocolate, the old South American way
s.how: Heat 500ml milk with a split red chilli and a cinnamon stick and steep 5 minutes off the heat. Strain, reheat and whisk in 120g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of flaky salt until smooth. Pour into tiny cups.

s.note: the window of the chocolate shop
s.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 250g chopped dark chocolate with 20g butter. Stir smooth and chill 3 hours. Scoop and roll into balls, then coat in cocoa, chopped toasted hazelnuts or sugar mixed with chilli flakes.

m.note: the birthday party Vianne cooks for Armande
m.how: Salt 4 duck legs overnight with thyme and garlic. Rinse, then cook slowly in their own fat at 140C for 2.5 hours. Roast 1kg potatoes in some of the fat at 200C. Crisp the legs skin side down and serve with a green salad.

w.note: the shop's chocolate, all of it
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 30g butter. Whisk in 4 yolks, then fold in 4 whites whipped with 40g sugar. Spoon into small cups and chill 4 hours. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt mixed with chilli flakes.

d.note: a French village after Lent ends
d.how: Pour a 750ml bottle of light southern French red into a saucepan with an orange cut into slices, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise, 4 cloves and 3 tbsp honey. Warm over low heat for 15 minutes without letting it boil. Strain into small heatproof glasses and add a fresh orange slice to each.
